request.message: im doing hanoi, then hue, then hoi an — what should i stop at along the way?

response.message:
good news, you've got saves spread across all three stops and a couple of strong ones on the legs between them. your list is actually pretty well balanced, so this is more about ordering and timing than filling gaps.

---

hanoi

you saved [Railway Tuan](kebi://venue/939ba8f5-e83b-4e64-9d3b-b1eeb00b096b) Cafe, the one on the street where the train runs through. the insider note on this one is specific: the 7pm train is the one worth being there for, and the cafes on the north section are looser about checking tickets. so time your evening around that, get there before 7, grab a coffee, and wait for it.

---

the hue leg

you've got a save in Hue that's time-sensitive. [Quan Hanh](kebi://venue/a3c3ca18-4041-4188-ad8d-9cf52df669bb) is a traditional spot you saved manually, cash only, and the banh loc (their thing) runs out by early evening. go before 6 or you'll miss it. worth building your first evening in Hue around.

---

hue to hoi an, this leg is the best part of the drive

two stops worth making on the way down.

[Kala Kala Beach Club](kebi://venue/a5a27bb2-d0ec-4b33-81a9-cb3baa1b9dc4) is one you saved from a TikTok, it's on the coast, and the note says sunset is the slot. daybeds book out on weekends, so if you're passing through on a weekday, arriving around 4pm is the move. on a weekend you'd want to book ahead.

also on this leg: [Motorvina Da Nang](kebi://venue/4892f6da-ab37-4df0-b4a7-a2b7e244ca98), a scooter rental place in Da Nang. someone shared content on this one, they do one-way rentals specifically for riding the Hai Van Pass, which is the mountain road between Da Nang and Hue. if you're up for it, rent there and ride the pass rather than sitting in a bus or car. one of the better stretches of road in Vietnam.

and [Bep Hen](kebi://venue/a853b835-5e9a-4169-a9ad-c4aa1c4175f4) is a Vietnamese restaurant you saved that sits on this leg too. closes between services, roughly 2 to 5pm, so plan for lunch or dinner, not a mid-afternoon drop-in.

---

hoi an

two saves here. [Roving Chill House](kebi://venue/743de441-cdee-4166-80a5-576215e31bcc) is the one to anchor an evening around, cocktails, outdoor seating, reservable. the note says go before 10, rice paddy light and no tour groups yet, so earlier in the evening is the call.

[Nu Eatery](kebi://venue/1965297d-4ab1-49a9-9084-723c9909d2ce) is your daytime spot, brunch and lunch, casual, outdoor. good for a slow morning.

---

the one question that changes how I'd lay this out: how many nights are you spending in each city? that decides whether Hue is a full day or a pass-through, and whether you're hitting Kala Kala on a weekday (easy) or a weekend (book ahead).
